claim: Skilled fast judgment needs two checkable conditions: a regular environment with valid cues, and enough practice with feedback on that environment. Without both, a correct first answer is luck. Basis is conceptual (two rival authors converged; Hogarth kind/wicked via a 2021 review); no new experiment.
agent_test: Define an S0 gate = task-class record with validity flag plus feedback log; compare gate-on vs always-deliberate on held-out kind and wicked task classes at equal tokens.

claim: Felt confidence in one answer does not separate skilled from heuristic intuition; it tracks story consistency, so it cannot be the trust test.
agent_test: Compare AUROC of verbalised confidence vs outcome-based task-class hit rate as predictors of first-answer correctness, per task class.

claim: Mechanical combination of the same cues beats or ties expert holistic combination in low-validity prediction tasks. Grove 2000 (via K&K, checked in K&K text): 136 studies, mechanical better in 63, tie 65, clinical better in 8. Kuncel 2013 (checked in paper): job performance r=.44 vs .28 (population estimate).
agent_test: On a prediction task class with fixed cues, compare the agent's holistic answer vs a fixed rubric or sum it fills in, at equal tokens.

claim: The formula advantage is small in mental health (Aegisdottir: d+=.12 on the strictest set; of 48 effects 52% favour formula, 38% tie, 10% favour clinician) and larger on some criteria (job performance, training).
agent_test: Do not assume a large formula edge; estimate it per task class on our own bench before adding a rubric step.

claim: Formulas win mainly because human judges apply cues inconsistently (noise), not because they lack insight: unique judge knowledge beyond a linear model is near zero (lens model C about 0); bootstrapped models of the judge beat the judge. Goldberg and Karelaia were only seen second-hand and the Noise book only in snippets.
agent_test: Run the agent twice on identical items and measure disagreement (noise); compare with a majority of its own prior runs.

claim: Familiarity with the setting and extra information did not help clinicians: they did better on data from outside their own setting (d+ .06 vs .14), and equal or more information did not close the gap. Cells are small and authors flag these as trends.
agent_test: Test whether retrieved same-task past cases help the agent on a task class with no feedback; expect no gain if the class is low-validity.

claim: Expertise is fractionated: the same professional is reliable on some tasks and not others (Shanteau lists, hail vs routine weather). The trust unit must be the task class, not the agent as a whole. Shanteau not opened, so both lines trace to K&K.
agent_test: Keep per-task-class hit-rate counters; test whether class-level gating beats one global fast/slow threshold at equal tokens.

claim: A mark of real expertise is noticing an anomaly or novel case and switching to deliberate search. K&K give no data on how well this works; it is where Klein and Kahneman differ in emphasis. Newer LLM work: refusal can be trained and carries over to other domains (R-Tuning), but surveys say abstention generalises poorly out of distribution and false-alarm cost is not quantified.
agent_test: Add a novelty check (distance to stored task-class cases) before the fast answer; measure escape rate on out-of-class items and false alarms.

claim: Slowing down is not shown to improve diagnosis: in 113 analysed residents correct diagnoses were faster than wrong ones (115 s vs 129 s, d=0.37) and held with more confidence; the bias induction failed, so the bias claim itself is untested.
agent_test: On our logs, check whether fast answers are right more often within a task class (control for item difficulty).

claim: Forecasting skill can be raised even in a low-validity domain when scoring and feedback are supplied: GJP training about 10%, teaming about 10%, recruitment about 10%; a smaller replication supports identifying top forecasters but with weaker training evidence. Mellers 2015 seen as abstract only. A 2025 item-response-theory reanalysis (abstract only) found the 2014 teaming and training effects shrank, vanished or reversed after controls; recruitment and persistence of top forecasters are not addressed by that abstract.
agent_test: Give the agent a scored forecast loop on a task class; test whether its record improves per-class trust vs an unscored loop.

claim: LLM verbalised confidence is often better calibrated than token probability for RLHF models (Tian: ECE cut by about half; GPT-4 TruthfulQA 0.445 to 0.082), but discrimination stays weak on hard sets (GPT-4 TruthfulQA AUC .632, ChatGPT .492). Other work finds verbalised confidence overconfident (Xiong: GPT-4 AUROC 62.7%). Kapoor 2024: on MMLU verbal elicitation discriminates about as well as weaker fine-tuned methods but is poorly calibrated; sampling agreement discriminates very weakly; a trained correctness classifier is better on both.
agent_test: Compare calibration and AUROC of verbalised confidence vs sampled agreement vs class hit rate on our task classes.

claim: Models show a hard-easy effect like humans (11 models, mean confidence 88% vs accuracy 79%), and reasoning models are far better calibrated than chat models (LifeEval ECE .037 vs .150).
agent_test: Track the hard-easy gap per task class; trust stated confidence only after class-level recalibration.

claim: More thinking tokens can worsen calibration and accuracy beyond a small budget (Gemini 2.5 Flash: accuracy 41.7 to 45.0 peak, 35.7 at 768 tokens; overconfidence up to +21.3 points) and inverse scaling in test-time compute appears on built tasks. Workshop-level and constructed tasks.
agent_test: Sweep thinking budget per task class; plot accuracy and overconfidence vs budget at equal total tokens.

claim: Without an outside correctness signal, asking the model to re-check its first answer does not help and often hurts (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after 5 calls); gains in earlier work came from oracle labels (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5 with oracle).
agent_test: Compare re-check with and without an outside check (test or tool) at equal tokens; expect gain only with the outside check.

claim: Agreement among sampled answers is a usable but imperfect trust signal and drives early-exit gating: ReASC -71.1% compute at 92.04 vs 92.12 accuracy (GSM8K, Gemma-3-4B), CGES -69.4% calls at equal accuracy. Gain over earlier adaptive self-consistency is smaller (ASC already -62.5%). Same-model samples share errors. Counter-evidence: Kapoor 2024 found sampling-based uncertainty discriminates very weakly on MMLU.
agent_test: Early-exit ladder: one answer, accept only if class record is good and samples agree; compare with fixed N samples at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought hurts on tasks where verbal deliberation hurts people (implicit pattern learning: GPT-4o -23.1 points; face recognition: GPT-4o -12.8) and helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks, so the fast path is better for some task classes. Apple puzzle study (2025): non-thinking beats thinking at low complexity, thinking wins at medium, both fail at high; complexity, not cue validity, was varied.
agent_test: Per task class compare direct vs CoT at equal tokens and let the class record choose the mode.

claim: Routers that pick fast or slow mode per item work but do not transfer across models: slow mode helped only 3.11% of items, and a router trained on one LLM lost accuracy on another. Small models, own-data training.
agent_test: Train the gate on our own per-class record, not generic features; test transfer to a new model.

claim: Human users trust LLM answers beyond the model's confidence; longer explanations raise confidence without better discrimination (AUC .54 vs .57).
agent_test: Relevant if the agent reads its own long reasoning back as evidence for its answer (G4); test by hiding the explanation from the gate.

claim: A learned estimate of whether an LLM answer is right needs on the order of 1000 graded examples to beat simple baselines and gains flatten after about 5000; no source gives a hit-rate floor or a sequential-test rule for skipping deliberation. Evidence is from fine-tuned 7B models on MMLU.
agent_test: Estimate per-class hit rate with a Wilson lower bound; sweep the number of graded cases (10, 30, 100, 300, 1000) and find where the bound-based gate matches the always-deliberate arm on accuracy.

claim: Within-agent noise is large even at temperature 0: five LLMs showed up to 15% accuracy change across 10 identical runs and best-to-worst gaps up to 70%, and it differs by task. A single first answer is one draw, so the fast-answer gate should use answer-level agreement over a few runs and measure noise per task class.
agent_test: Run each item 5 times at default settings; log answer-agreement per task class; test whether low-noise classes have higher first-answer hit rate.

claim: In-context learning from labelled examples is a weak channel for learning the input-to-label relation on easy classification (random labels cost 0-5% absolute in 2022 models) but noisy labels clearly hurt on text generation. So the task-class track record should live in the harness as a counter, not be left to in-context learning. Delay and ambiguity of labels were not tested by any source found.
agent_test: Compare a harness-held per-class hit rate against showing the agent its own past graded cases in context, with clean, 30% noisy, and delayed grades.

claim: No source tests whether the mode choice (direct vs reasoning) follows task validity. The best available map for 2025 models is by complexity: direct mode wins on low-complexity puzzles, reasoning at medium, both fail at high; this map is contested and was not built on cue validity.
agent_test: Build a small per-class table of direct vs reasoning accuracy at equal tokens, with tasks ordered by cue validity and by complexity separately.

claim: Estimating the validity of a new task class before outcomes arrive has no tested method; the only evidence is for people, where non-accuracy proxies for forecaster skill correlate with accuracy at median r of about 0.20. Tetlock-style multi-year feedback remains the only strong answer.
agent_test: Test whether 3-5 early graded cases plus a shuffled-cue check give any rank correlation with the later class hit rate.

claim: The task-class gate must come with an out-of-class alarm, but no source measures how often an LLM agent detects that an item is outside its class or the cost of false alarms. Training a refusal skill is possible and transfers (R-Tuning) and a trained correctness estimator transferred across formats (Kapoor), yet surveys say abstention generalises poorly out of distribution.
agent_test: Inject out-of-class items at known rates into each class; report detection rate, false-alarm rate, and tokens wasted by false alarms.
